title: Baron’s first assertions: all sin mortal of itself; reprobate sins mortal; elect atrocious sins still deadly
source_text: XXXV. Nam jam dicta Disputatione parte prima, Sessione secunda, haec est ejus assertio prima, Omne peccatum ex se est mortale, nullumque est veniale, nisi per ac-cidens. 2. Omnia peccata reproborum peccata sunt mortalia: ideoque non tantum ex merito, sed etiam ab eventu. 3. Etsi omnia reproborum peccata sunt mortalia, non tamen e contrario dicendum est omnia electorum peccata esse venialia. Nam, inquit, peccata eorundem atrocia, & conscientiam vastantia non solum merentur exclusionem a favore Dei, & a regno coelesti; sed etiam ab eo favoris gradu, quo antea a Deo diligebantur, eos actu excludunt, & si in iis perseverarent, eos e regno coelesti in aeternum excluderent. De quibus peccatis Scriptura affirmative docet, quod quicunque ea facit regni coelestis, & vitae aeternae particeps esse nequeat, 1 Cor. 6. & alibi; & Deum odisse & abominari qui talia faciunt, Prov. 6. & 22.
pass_a_gloss: For in the already mentioned Disputation, part one, second Session, this is his first assertion: Every sin is of itself mortal, and none is venial except by accident. 2. All sins of the reprobate are mortal sins: and therefore not only from desert, but also from the event. 3. Although all sins of the reprobate are mortal, yet it is not to be said on the contrary that all sins of the elect are venial. For, he says, their atrocious sins that waste the conscience not only merit exclusion from God’s favor and from the heavenly kingdom; but also actually exclude them from that degree of favor by which they were formerly loved by God, and if they persevered in them would exclude them forever from the heavenly kingdom. Concerning which sins Scripture affirmatively teaches that whoever does them cannot be a partaker of the heavenly kingdom and of eternal life, 1 Cor. 6 and elsewhere; and that God hates and abominates those who do such things, Prov. 6 and 22.
pass_b_english: Baron’s opening axioms: no venial sin by nature; reprobate sins mortal both by desert and by event.
Elect atrocious, conscience-wasting falls still actually cut favor-degree and would forever shut heaven if persevered in—against flat ‘all elect sins are venial.’

choices.why: Blocks the slide from ‘reprobate sins mortal’ to ‘elect sins all venial’.
